record.paper_title: Some open problems on the analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
record.original_question: For the Cauchy-Fueter system P(D)f = 0, give a geometric characterization of the open sets that are P-convex. In the source, P-convexity is the weaker hypothesis that replaces ordinary convexity in the Ehrenpreis-Palamodov exactness theorem for systems of linear constant-coefficient differential operators, and it should express an appropriate relation between the system P and the topology of the open set.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the algebra of quaternions and consider the Cauchy–Fueter operator in $n$ variables. For a quaternionic variable $q = x_0 + x_1 i + x_2 j + x_3 k$, define
$$\bar\partial_{CF} = \frac{\partial}{\partial x_0} + i\frac{\partial}{\partial x_1} + j\frac{\partial}{\partial x_2} + k\frac{\partial}{\partial x_3}.$$
For $n$ quaternionic variables $q_1,\dots,q_n$, let $P(D)$ be the linear constant-coefficient differential operator (with values in a suitable free $\mathbb{H}$-module) whose components are $\bar\partial_{CF,\ell}$ ($\ell=1,\dots,n$), so that the homogeneous system $P(D)f = 0$ on an open set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^{4n}$ characterizes regular (Fueter-regular) functions of several quaternionic variables.

Recall that, in the Ehrenpreis–Palamodov theory of systems of linear partial differential operators with constant coefficients, an open set $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is called $P$-convex (for the system $P$) if the cohomology of the associated complex on $\Omega$ vanishes in the appropriate degrees—equivalently, the exactness theorem that holds for convex $\Omega$ continues to hold for $\Omega$. $P$-convexity is strictly weaker than ordinary convexity and is expected to reflect a compatibility between the system $P$ and the topology/geometry of $\Omega$.

Problem. Give a purely geometric characterization of the open sets $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^{4n}$ that are $P$-convex for the Cauchy–Fueter system in $n$ quaternionic variables.
artifact.status_search_result: A complete geometric characterization of P-convex open sets is known only in restricted settings (e.g., scalar principal-type operators in ℝ³ with C²-boundary). For general systems, and in particular for the Cauchy–Fueter system in several quaternionic variables, no such geometric characterization appears in the literature, and the problem is still regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: The Cauchy problem at simply characteristic points and P-convexity
status_evidence.snippet: A complete geometric characterization of P-convex sets in R^3 has been given when P is of principal type and Ω has C^2-boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Geometric characterizations of P-convex sets exist only in special cases (scalar principal-type operators in R^3), not for general systems such as Cauchy–Fueter.

status_evidence.title: Cauchy-Fueter system in several variables
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of analysis of the Cauchy-Fueter system in several quaternionic variables and associated open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Analytical questions about the Cauchy–Fueter system in several variables, including P-convexity, are studied as open problems.
